sourceBindings.text: Use the documented FJ500-SER as an example of a manufacturer maintenance plan. The trainer must match the real machine, manual, operator eligibility and site before practical work. A symptom is a reason to stop and investigate safely, not permission to test a live fault.

If eligible and trained, perform permitted post-use cleaning and inspection on a stopped, isolated, cooled, matched machine under a trainer, and identify manual-specific air-cleaner, oil, tine and storage actions that require a qualified technician.

Explain at least two plausible causes and safe next decisions for non-start and ineffective cultivation, and stop/report dangerous vibration or control difficulty rather than diagnose by touching moving parts.

Prepare an honest model-specific use, inspection and fault report with the manufacturer's interval, individual observation status, referral and follow-up, and use self-reflection without claiming a skill pass.

sourceBindings.text: On an inert illustrated machine, order normal stop, anti-start isolation, cooling, accessible cleaning, visible checks, report and technician referral. Assign the Honda printed 40–41 schedule to actual hours rather than a made-up weekly interval.

Solve the original no-start, ineffective-weeding and unusual-vibration cases. Give two possible cause/remedy pairs for each of the first two, mark immediate stop conditions, and distinguish checks the learner may make from qualified service.

Only for an eligible trained learner and matched actual machine/site, individually perform permitted post-use care under the trainer; otherwise annotate an inert demonstration and leave practical C01 unattempted. Complete the source card and added model-specific record.
Return the learner to the exact unsafe or unsupported action and allow a reasoned retry.

This is knowledge rehearsal and an unsigned draft record. The owner has confirmed the planned cohort meets the age condition. Actual machine/manual, instruction, permitted task scope, site and each learner’s observed actions still need trainer verification. No online result awards practical C01 or permission to restart.

sourceBindings.text: Can I explain when care must stop and who may operate?
Can I carry out only the permitted cleaning/inspection actions on an isolated matched machine?
Can I report symptoms, service interval and referral truthfully?
Can I identify which action still needs practice or observation by the trainer?
Use this self-assessment to identify what to review or practise next. Your choice is not evidence of practical competence or a trainer assessment.

The cultivator reflection is an added learning aid; the original final table has no cultivator row. Its original column order is can/cannot/partly. The added interface may order those three choices differently; none is a practical result.

sourceBindings.text: anti-start isolation
The matched manual's means of preventing unexpected engine/tine motion before inspection or cleaning.
air cleaner
The intake filter assembly; foam and paper elements have different manufacturer service methods.
service interval
A maker-specified calendar or operating-hour point for inspection or maintenance, often whichever comes first.
fault report
A record of symptom, observed conditions, safe checks, action, referral and follow-up without invented diagnosis.
excessive vibration
An abnormal shaking requiring immediate safe stop and diagnosis only after isolation.
eligible operator
A trained person permitted by the machine manual and applicable rules to perform a supervised practical action.
